rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A midrange temperature leaves room to probe temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

All pairs have excess resolution, so halve the gradient duration to reduce the time penalty. Keeping the solvent endpoints and temperature fixed reveals how the critical cluster responds to gradient steepness.

The faster gradient removes the time penalty but compresses a critical cluster. Raise temperature while keeping the gradient fixed to test whether temperature-dependent selectivity can resolve that cluster without lengthening the run.

Use an intermediate temperature to avoid the new near-coelution at 60 C, with a slightly shallower gradient to improve the central cluster. This should retain much of the speed advantage while targeting full resolution.

Increase temperature by 5 C to separate the remaining critical pair while preserving the zero time penalty. This intermediate setting may also retain adequate separation for the pair that nearly coeluted at 60 C.

The maximum CRF is already reached; retain injection 5 as the benchmark. This narrower gradient preserves its slope and extends beyond the estimated last-peak elution fraction of 0.57, testing whether the same maximum score can be maintained with a lower final organic fraction.

With the maximum CRF secured, test a slightly shallower gradient for a larger minimum-resolution margin. The modest slope change should keep the last peak near 8 minutes while revealing whether either critical pair improves or approaches coelution.

Test a higher starting organic fraction at the successful gradient slope to shorten retention and probe selectivity in the two marginally resolved pairs. Keep injection 5 as the maximum-score benchmark if this change sacrifices resolution.

Make the gradient shallower to recover separation of the early critical pair while retaining the time savings from the higher starting organic fraction. This may achieve the maximum CRF with a slightly better minimum-resolution margin.

Slightly reduce the gradient slope from injection 9 to improve its limiting pair while keeping the last peak close to the zero-time-penalty boundary. The final organic fraction remains above the estimated last-peak elution fraction, so all compounds should still elute during the gradient.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction combined with a shallower gradient can improve the minimum-resolution margin while preserving the maximum CRF. This extends the successful compensation between starting composition and slope seen in injections 8–10.

The maximum score is secured, so explore a distinct low-temperature selectivity regime rather than further compressing the narrow 55 C optimum. Comparing directly with injection 2 will test whether cooling separates the central cluster while keeping the last peak within the zero-time-penalty window.

Test a faster, high-temperature regime with a higher starting organic fraction to move beyond the selectivity crossover that caused near-coelution in injection 3. This explores a potentially shorter fully resolved method while retaining the existing CRF 1.000 methods as benchmarks.

Raise the starting organic fraction to shift the remaining critical pair farther beyond its selectivity crossover, while reducing the slope to preserve separation elsewhere. Monitor the first pair closely because its retention and resolution may decrease at the higher starting strength.

Return to the starting composition that preserved early-peak resolution and test a modestly steeper gradient than injection 13. This probes whether the remaining selectivity crossover can be cleared before the adjacent pair becomes limiting; the established CRF 1.000 methods remain the benchmarks.

Test a moderately cooler selectivity regime with a slope between injections 1 and 2, seeking separation on the opposite side of the central-pair crossover. The maximum CRF is already secured; this tests for an alternative optimum without the severe crowding observed at 25 C.

Return to the maximum-score region and slightly flatten the gradient relative to injection 10 to improve the earlier critical pair. The last peak should remain near the observed zero-time-penalty boundary, while the later critical pair is expected to change little.

Flatten the gradient relative to injection 11 to recover its limiting pair while preserving the stronger separation of the later critical pair. This tests whether a larger minimum-resolution margin is available, although the longer retention may introduce a small time penalty; retain the established maximum-score methods.

Slightly flatten the gradient from injection 18 to bring its limiting resolution above 1.5 while retaining the later pair’s margin. The last peak is expected near 9 minutes, testing whether this starting composition can also achieve the maximum CRF before a time penalty appears.

Test a shallower gradient at 60 C to separate the pair that nearly coeluted in injection 3, while preserving the favorable separation elsewhere at this temperature. This may reveal another maximum-score region; the validated 55 C methods remain the benchmarks.

Refine the established maximum-score region with a slightly shallower gradient than injection 17. This should widen the earlier critical pair while keeping the later pair above 1.5 and the last peak below the approximately 9-minute time-penalty boundary.

Test a slightly steeper gradient than injection 5 to locate the fastest edge of the maximum-score region. The earlier critical pair may become limiting, so retain the validated CRF 1.000 methods if this small acceleration sacrifices resolution.

Preserve injection 5’s successful slope through the critical cluster, then hold at a lower final organic fraction. This tests whether the maximum CRF can be retained with less organic solvent; the isolated final peak will elute during the hold and may incur a time penalty.

Refine the validated 55 C region with a slightly shallower gradient than injection 21 and a lower final organic fraction. The critical pairs should remain resolved, with the last peak expected near 9 minutes; retain the existing maximum-score methods if a time penalty appears.

Use the final injection to test a slightly shallower slope at the edge of the established maximum-score region, targeting full resolution with the last peak near 9 minutes. The campaign has already reached the theoretical maximum CRF of 1.000; retain injection 5 as the benchmark.
